Architecture Overview

1. Memory-First Architecture
  • Ignite's primary storage tier is RAM; data is kept in off-heap memory regions managed outside the JVM heap to avoid GC pauses;
  • The off-heap memory is organized into fixed-size pages (default 4 KB); pages hold data entries, indexes, and metadata;
  • This page-based memory architecture is called the Durable Memory (or PageMemory) layer;
  • It behaves like a virtual memory system: pages in RAM can optionally be backed by pages on disk (Native Persistence);
2. Node Types
  • Server Node
    • Participates in data storage, caching, compute, SQL processing, and streaming;
    • By default a node starts as a server;
    • Forms the backbone of the cluster; all data is partitioned among server nodes;
  • Client Node
    • Joins the cluster topology as a full member (receives topology updates, discovery events);
    • Does not store data; forwards requests to server nodes;
    • Useful for applications that need full API access (compute, transactions, continuous queries);
    • Configured via: IgniteConfiguration.setClientMode(true);
  • Thin Client
    • Connects over a lightweight TCP protocol; does not join the topology;
    • Much smaller footprint than a client node — no discovery overhead;
    • Supports key-value, SQL, compute (Ignite 2.16+), and continuous queries;
    • Available in Java, .NET, C++, Python, Node.JS, PHP;
3. Data Distribution
  • Every cache is divided into a fixed number of partitions (1024 by default);
  • Each partition is assigned to a primary node and zero or more backup nodes via the affinity function;
  • When a key-value pair is written, Ignite hashes the key to determine which partition it belongs to, then routes the operation to the primary node of that partition;
  • If the primary node goes down, one of the backup nodes is automatically promoted to primary;
4. Multi-Tier Storage
  • Ignite supports a multi-tier storage model:
    • Off-Heap Memory (Tier 1) — primary storage; managed by PageMemory outside the JVM heap;
    • Native Persistence (Tier 2) — data is written to disk in the same page format; survives full cluster restarts;
    • 3rd-Party Persistence (Tier 3) — Ignite can read-through / write-through to an external database (RDBMS, Cassandra, etc.) via the CacheStore interface;
  • You can use any combination of tiers: memory-only, memory + native persistence, memory + external DB, or all three;
5. Discovery and Communication
  • Ignite uses two network subsystems:
    • Discovery — responsible for detecting nodes joining and leaving the cluster; used by TCP/IP Discovery or ZooKeeper Discovery;
    • Communication — responsible for direct point-to-point messaging between nodes (data replication, compute task execution, SQL query distribution);
  • Discovery forms a logical ring; communication uses direct TCP connections;
6. High-Level Component Map
  • ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                   Application Layer                  │
│  (Thin Client / Client Node / Embedded Server Node)  │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│        Key-Value API  │  SQL Engine  │  Compute Grid │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                  Data Grid (Caches)                   │
│       Partitioning │ Replication │ Transactions       │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│          Durable Memory (Off-Heap PageMemory)         │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Native Persistence  │  External CacheStore (RDBMS)   │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│        Discovery (TCP / ZooKeeper) │ Communication    │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
